section.title: The ooSQLFunction Class
section.para: An ooSQLFunction object represents a SQL function or aggregate of an ooSQLite package, written in C or C++, that a package describes in its function table, with its number of arguments. The C code stays in the shared library of the package; the object holds what ooSQLite needs to register it: its name and its entry points. Programs do not create ooSQLFunction objects: ooSQLite creates them.

The object is obtained with the getFunction method of an ooSQLPackage object, and its only use is as the argument of the createFunction method of the ooSQLiteConnection class, which registers the function on the connection under the name given there, with the number of arguments of the package unless another one is given. The same object can be registered on any number of connections, and under different names. register registers all the functions of a package at once, and autoFunction makes one automatic.

row.entry: Creates the object. Used internally by ooSQLite.

section.title: new (Class method)
section.para: Creates an ooSQLFunction object. ooSQLite uses it internally; programs obtain the object with the getFunction method of an ooSQLPackage object.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
entry [required]
A Buffer object with a copy of the description that the package gives in C. Only ooSQLite can create it.
A Rexx program can not create the Buffer object that new needs, so new invoked from a program raises a syntax error: 88.901 without an argument, and 88.900 with any other argument.

&changed11;A subclass of ooSQLFunction whose init method does not forward to the init method of ooSQLFunction creates objects that are not initialized. createFunction raises an execution error, 98.900, when it is given one. Before ooSQLite 1.1 it crashed the interpreter.

This example registers the half function of the examplePackage package on two connections, under two names:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplePackage') function = package~getFunction('half') db2 = .ooSQLiteConnection~new(':memory:') say db~createFunction('half', function) say db2~createFunction('mitad', function) say db~exec("SELECT half(9) AS h;", .true)[1]['H'] say db2~exec("SELECT mitad(9) AS m;", .true)[1]['M'] db2~close /* Output: 0 0 4.5 4.5 */

Invoking new from a program raises a syntax error:
signal on syntax function = .ooSQLFunction~new('half') say 'not reached' syntax: say condition('O')~code condition('O')~message /* Output: 88.900 Argument 1 must be of the Buffer class; found half. */

An object of a subclass whose init method does not forward to the init method of ooSQLFunction is not initialized:
signal on syntax say db~createFunction('half', .myFunction~new) say 'not reached' syntax: say condition('O')~code parse value condition('O')~message with head ': ' reason say head say reason /* Output: 98.900 this ooSQLFunction object was not initialized the init method of a subclass must forward to the init method of ooSQLFunction. */ ::class myFunction subclass ooSQLFunction ::method init nop
